questions.stem: A user must transfer a single 5 GB video file between a Windows PC and a MacBook using one USB flash drive. Which file system should the drive use?
questions.explanation: exFAT is cross-platform across Windows, macOS, and Linux and was designed specifically for flash drives to lift FAT32's 4 GB single-file cap.
questions.trap: FAT32 is also cross-platform, but any single file is capped at 4 GB, so a 5 GB video will not transfer.

questions.stem: Which workstation OS does the transcript single out as the number-one target for cyber attackers, and why?

choices.text: Windows, because of its massive market share and industry support
macOS, because it is closed source and runs on premium hardware
Linux, because it is open source and lacks a central support company
Chrome OS, because it depends on a constant internet connection

questions.explanation: Windows is the market leader, and that popularity is exactly what makes it the most-targeted OS for attackers.
questions.trap: Being closed source does not make macOS the biggest target; targeting follows market share, and Windows has the largest share.

questions.stem: A school wants a lightweight workstation OS built on the Linux kernel where most applications run inside a browser and a constant internet connection is expected. Which OS fits best?
questions.explanation: Chrome OS is Google's lightweight, browser-centric workstation OS built on Linux that relies on a constant internet connection for its cloud-based apps.
questions.trap: Android is also Linux-based, but it is a mobile OS, not a workstation OS.

questions.stem: Which file system is the default on modern Macs and iPhones, optimized for the solid-state storage in those devices?
questions.explanation: APFS (Apple File System) is the modern default on macOS and iOS/iPadOS and is optimized for the SSDs used in current Apple hardware.
questions.trap: exFAT is for cross-platform flash drives, not the OS's primary file system. NTFS is a Windows default, not Apple.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs a file system known for handling very large data files efficiently in high-performance environments. Which is the best choice?
questions.explanation: XFS is the high-performance Linux file system the transcript highlights for handling very large data files efficiently.
questions.trap: ext4 is the common default on Linux desktops, but the transcript specifically calls out XFS for high performance and very large files.

questions.stem: Which FAT32 limitation was exFAT specifically designed to overcome?

choices.text: The 4 GB maximum size for any single file
A limit on the number of primary partitions per drive

questions.explanation: FAT32 caps any single file at 4 GB. exFAT was designed for flash drives to support much larger files while keeping cross-platform compatibility.
questions.trap: FAT32 is actually highly cross-platform; lack of compatibility is not what exFAT was created to fix.

questions.stem: Which mobile OS is open source, ships on devices from many manufacturers, and is maintained by the Open Handset Alliance?
questions.explanation: Android is the open-source mobile OS maintained by the Open Handset Alliance and shipped by many different hardware manufacturers.
questions.trap: iOS and iPadOS only run on Apple hardware and are not open source. Chrome OS is a workstation OS, not a phone OS.

questions.stem: A vendor has declared a workstation OS to be end of life (EOL). What is the primary security risk of continuing to run it?

choices.text: It no longer receives security updates from the vendor
It will refuse to boot once the EOL date passes
It loses cross-platform compatibility with other operating systems
It can no longer open standard data files like documents or images

questions.explanation: When an OS reaches EOL, the vendor stops issuing security updates, leaving any newly discovered vulnerabilities permanently unpatched.
questions.trap: EOL does not disable the OS; it keeps running and that is exactly why it is risky.

questions.stem: A user copies a Windows .exe installer to a Mac and double-clicks it. What is the expected result, per the compatibility rule for executables?

choices.text: It runs but in a sandboxed read-only mode
It runs through macOS's built-in Windows compatibility layer
It will not run, because application executables are OS-specific
It runs only if the Mac uses an APFS-formatted volume

questions.explanation: Application executables are OS-specific. A Windows .exe will not run natively on macOS or Linux without third-party translation software.
questions.trap: macOS does not include a built-in Windows compatibility layer; .exe files simply cannot execute natively there.

questions.stem: An organization standardizes on a web-based productivity suite. Which workstation operating systems can run this software?

choices.text: Only Windows, because of its industry support
Any OS that has a compatible web browser
Only macOS and Linux, because Windows blocks SaaS in the browser
Only Chrome OS, because the apps are cloud-based

questions.explanation: The transcript's compatibility rule says web-based apps work in any browser, which makes the underlying OS irrelevant for those apps.
questions.trap: The OS-specific rule applies to executables, not to web apps. Web apps are not locked to one OS or to Chrome OS.
